summary: I grew up inside a school. My mother was the principal, my father the chairperson, and I was the kid on campus before the first bell and still there after the last one. So when I say I build AI for Indian classrooms, it's not just a market I researched. It's where I come from. I studied Engineering Physics at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, then started a master's in theoretical physics at King's College London. Somewhere in that year, AI stopped being a research topic and became something that could solve realworld problems at a pace nothing else ever has. And I knew exactly which problem I wanted to solve. So I came back to the classrooms I grew up in. The problem I care about: a teacher in most Indian schools isn't teaching one class. Across sections, they're responsible for 100 to 150 students. Personalised attention at that scale is physically impossible for one person, and the tools teachers get rarely fit into how they actually work. At KoKo Ed I lead product. We build classroom intelligence systems for schools. On one side, state of the art tools that help teachers prepare and deliver their best classes. On the other, analytics that show them what's actually working for each student. The goal is simple, to give teachers their time back for what actually matters, which is teaching. Day to day: product architecture, AI systems, backend engineering, and a lot of time in schools. I believe every student deserves to experience great teaching and mentorship at least once. It can change the entire trajectory of a life. Our job is to help teachers and schools rise to that standard. Happy to connect with educators, school leaders, and builders working on AI in education.
